title: Hold the attempt in a finalizing phase after complete_task
description:
Objective: stop a session starting its next task before the previous task's bytes are landed. Today packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/completeTask.ts moves the task to REVIEW, frees the worker and returns a next action inviting more work, while the wrapper only lands after the CLI exits. A session can therefore begin task B while task A's artifact boundary is still open.

Deliverable: complete_task moves the owning attempt to phase finalizing instead of closing it, and its returned nextAction no longer tells the worker to claim or wait for more work while an attempt of theirs is finalizing. A coding claim by that worker is refused with a named, retryable reason naming the finalizing attempt.

Not in scope: the tool the runner calls to acknowledge the boundary, which is the sibling finalize task; the delivery-evidence gate on DONE; and any wrapper change. Do not alter the existing verification-object validation or the REVIEW transition itself.

This task unskips the acceptance case "fast QA cannot finish before candidate preparation" is not this one; it unskips nothing. The finalize sibling owns that case.

Verification: npx vitest run src/tools/completeTask.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: complete_task sets the owning attempt to phase finalizing and leaves it open
The nextAction returned by complete_task does not direct the worker to claim or wait for another task while one of their attempts is finalizing
A claim_next_task call from a worker holding a finalizing attempt is refused with a named retryable reason that identifies the attempt
The existing complete_task behaviour is unchanged: verification evidence validation, the completed-step check, the REVIEW transition and completionSummary persistence keep their current tests green
npx vitest run src/tools/completeTask.test.ts src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: Do not weaken or bypass the existing verification-evidence validation in util/enforcement.ts.
The refusal must be retryable and clearly worded; a wrapper reading it must not treat it as a fatal error.

implementationPlan.description: HOLD THE ATTEMPT IN FINALIZING INSTEAD OF LEAVING IT RUNNING. In src/tools/completeTask.ts, after every existing assertion passes and BEFORE the `updateTask` that moves the task to REVIEW, look up the task's current attempt with `currentAttempt` and, when one exists, move it to the finalizing phase through the store's `setAttemptPhase`. The ordering is the whole point and needs a comment saying so: the REVIEW transition is what frees the worker, so an attempt still in the running phase at that instant is exactly the window where a session starts task B while task A's bytes are unlanded. Doing it first means a later failure leaves a conservatively finalizing attempt on a still-WORKING task, which blocks only that worker's next claim and is repaired by its own retry — the opposite ordering would leave a freed worker with a running attempt, which is the defect. State plainly in the comment that this is not a cross-entity transaction and promises no rollback. A task with no attempt is a legacy row: skip silently, never throw, since rows created before attempts existed must keep completing. Then change the returned nextAction: when an attempt was moved to finalizing, return an object carrying only a reason that tells the worker to record its handoff note and exit so the wrapper can land the bytes, with no tool or args keys at all, because naming any claim or wait tool is the invitation this task exists to remove. Surface the attempt id and generation on the response using the same flat key names the claim result uses. Leave the verification-evidence validation, the completed-step check, the REVIEW transition, completionSummary persistence, the branch policy block and the chat post exactly as they are.

1. Imports (lines 6-7): `{ currentAttempt, setAttemptPhase }` from '../state/attemptStore.js' plus the `ExecutionAttempt` type. Nothing else in that module is pulled in — deliberately NOT `closeOpenAttempts`, so this tool has no reach for the terminal phase.

      const openAttempt = currentAttempt(state, task.id);
      const finalizing: ExecutionAttempt | null = openAttempt
        ? await setAttemptPhase(state, openAttempt.id, 'finalizing')
        : null;
   The 19-line comment above it states the ordering argument (the REVIEW write is what frees the worker, so a still-`running` attempt at that instant IS the defect window), spells out that going first fails safe (a later failure leaves a conservatively finalizing attempt on a still-WORKING task, blocking only this worker and repaired by its own retry), says plainly this is NOT a cross-entity transaction and promises no rollback, and records why `closed` is never used here (terminal in the store; closing hands the seat straight back). The `: null` arm is the legacy row — `currentAttempt` returns null for a task predating attempts, nothing throws.

3. The response (lines ~193-217): `...(finalizing ? { attemptId: finalizing.id, generation: finalizing.generation } : {})` — the same flat key names the claim result uses, siblings of `stats`, never nested. `nextAction` is now a ternary on `finalizing`: the finalizing arm is an object with ONLY a `reason` (no `tool`, no `args`) telling the worker its bytes are not landed until the session exits, to record the Serena handoff note, to end its turn, and that a claim from it is refused meanwhile; the null arm keeps the OLD `moe.wait_for_task` hint byte-identical for legacy rows, which is what the no-attempt test pins.

implementationPlan.description: REFUSE A CODING CLAIM WHILE THAT WORKER HAS AN ATTEMPT FINALIZING. Add one exported code-name constant to src/util/claimGuards.ts beside the existing refusal names, with a short comment explaining that the seat is not free until the boundary is acknowledged. Keep that module pure: it imports no StateManager today and must not start, so the lookup itself lives in the claim tool. In src/tools/claimNextTask.ts, inside the exclusive section and alongside the existing one-task-per-worker check — before any ranking, eligibility scan or assignment write — scan the attempts for one belonging to this workerId in the finalizing phase, using the store's list function rather than reaching into the state map directly. When one is found, return the same non-throwing refusal shape the existing alreadyAssigned path uses: `hasNext:false`, the stable code name, and a payload naming the attempt id, its generation and its task, plus a clearly worded message and a nextAction explaining that the attempt must be acknowledged and that retrying afterwards is expected. Do NOT throw: a task rail requires a wrapper reading this to treat it as retryable rather than fatal, and the throwing refusals in this file are reserved for genuine races. Guard on the worker id being present, so a caller supplying none keeps today's behavior. Change nothing about claimable statuses, dependency gating, ranking, the alreadyAssigned resume or the attempt opening the sibling task added. Re-run the two named test files; every case from step 2 must now pass.

WIRE SHAPE of the refusal (for QA and for wrapper authors):
  { hasNext: false,
    code: 'CLAIM_ATTEMPT_FINALIZING',
    finalizingAttempt: { attemptId, generation, taskId },
    message: 'Worker <id> still holds attempt <attemptId> (generation <n>) on task <taskId> in phase finalizing: its bytes are not landed yet, so no new task may be started. This is a retryable refusal, NOT a fatal error.',

The finalizing attempt has to be acknowledged before you take another task; once it is, claiming again is expected to succeed, so retry rather than escalate. A release, a deregister or a daemon restart also clears it.' } }

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN CHANGE AND IT IS FIXED. Only claimNextTask.ts changed in this step (the refusal's nextAction text); no logic moved.

THE FINDING. My first refusal message told the reader "A release, a deregister or a daemon restart also clears it." I went and read all four close paths instead of trusting the plan's wording, and ALL THREE of those are FALSE:
- workerStore.deleteWorker:261 filters `if (task.assignedWorkerId !== workerId) continue;`
- workerLifecycle.releaseWorkerTasks does the same
- workerStore.purgeAllWorkers:344 only visits tasks where `task.assignedWorkerId && isTaskAssignedToMissingWorker(task)`
- releaseTask returns early at :225-233 ("Task already unassigned") and never reaches its closeOpenAttempts at :338
complete_task leaves the task REVIEW and UNASSIGNED, so every one of those filters misses it. An operator following my text would have deregistered, seen nothing change, and lost time. Rewritten to the verified truth: the attempt is closed by the NEXT CLAIM of that task — openClaimAttempt arm 3 at claimNextTask.ts:62 calls closeOpenAttempts before opening its own — which in practice is QA picking the task up for review, and the message now says plainly that deregister/release/restart do NOT clear it and why.

BLAST RADIUS, measured not assumed. MOE_WORKER_ID is one id per wrapper RUN (moe-agent.ps1:325, moe-agent.sh:608), not per task, so a seat that completes task A is refused every claim until someone claims A. The feature still achieves its purpose on the normal path — CLI exits, wrapper lands the bytes, next claim is refused only until QA picks A up — but the refusal outlives the landing, because nothing acknowledges it. That is the accepted dead end of this slice and it is now named in the runtime message itself, not just in a note.
